July 4th— How pleasing is it to receive even the least testimony of gratitude from a slave, for my part I think I have
so much injured that I never feel as if I had a claim to their affection or voluntary good offices— Just now I gave
harry the key of the milk house to get out some butter to drop Tabby's rabbit for her, it being one of the
dog had caught a bright day, I after wards, as it was the conclusion of harvest I had worked hard all
day, sent him tea biscuit & butter for their supper, aiders as I gave them to harry, now with Tabby's
rabbits you will have a nice supper, she went out with this message, but when she delivered it, it shant be fixed, said Tabby,
no, no, added the other, we wont eat it but save it for your son, as it is a rarity—
It has most sweet with this rabbit taste to me, thus reasoned with the good will of
these poor slaves.—
During the last week or two, I have had my feelings almost agitated at the sight of the suffering of one of these unfortunate
creatures— Lizzie, a fine, good natured, active young Man, had been hewed by Mr Smith most of last winter; in the spring his master died
to be used as for sale by the executor. He solicited Mr Smith to buy him, but the interest seconded his request, my excellent hus-
band would not sacrifice his principles, which were all adverse to slavery.— He was bought
